2608.06377.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
2608.06377.paper_summary: Language models increasingly condition their answers on external signals, and a single misleading one can turn a correct answer wrong. The obvious remedy, training models to resist such signals, hides a failure mode: a model that ignores all context looks robust yet is useless when the context is worth trusting. We recast the problem as selective trust and introduce MIST, a human-annotated benchmark that renders each reasoning item under four matched conditions (clean, misleading, correct-context, and irrelevant-context), together with SC2W, a paired metric counting how often a misleading signal flips a clean-correct answer to wrong. Across a comprehensive benchmark study, we observe that such a susceptibility is universal. We then propose SCOPE, which mines clean-correct/misleading-wrong failures and optimizes a standard Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) objective over matched preference pairs balanced equally across all four conditions, rather than over misleading items alone. Our approach substantially reduces SC2W on popular open-sourced models while preserving accuracy when the added context is clean, correct, or irrelevant. With this work, we argue that models should be judged on selective trust, not on resistance alone.
2608.06377.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型越來越多地根據外部信號來調整其回答，而單一的誤導性信號就能將正確的答案變為錯誤。明顯的解決辦法是訓練模型抵抗這些信號，但這隱藏了一種失效模式：一個忽略所有上下文的模型看似穩健，但在上下文值得信任時卻毫無用處。我們將問題重新表述為選擇性信任，並引入MIST，一個人類標註的基準，將每個推理項目置於四種匹配條件下（乾淨、誤導、正確上下文和無關上下文），以及SC2W，一個配對指標，計算誤導性信號將乾淨正確答案翻轉為錯誤的頻率。在一項全面的基準研究中，我們觀察到這種脆弱性是普遍存在的。然後我們提出SCOPE，該方法挖掘乾淨正確/誤導錯誤的失敗，並在所有四種條件下平衡的匹配偏好對上優化標準的直接偏好優化（DPO）目標，而不是僅僅針對誤導項目。我們的方法在流行的開源模型上大幅減少了SC2W，同時在添加的上下文為乾淨、正確或無關時保持準確性。通過這項工作，我們主張模型應該根據選擇性信任來評價，而不僅僅是抵抗能力。
